title: Raw NWB units-table waveform_duration/PT_ratio/waveform_halfwidth are uninterpretable on this corpus -- not just unit-ambiguous, likely broken upstream of jnwb
notes: Found while building the waveform-feature portion of the neuron-type/layer/LFP supplemental analysis (goal-neuron-type-layer-lfp-relationships-20260815). Plan's own verification gate required confirming waveform_duration's physical unit before trusting a narrow/broad-spiking cutoff derived from it -- this check FAILED rather than passed.

Direct read of sub-C31o_ses-230816_rec.nwb's units table (h5py, first 200 units): waveform_duration ranges 0.0274706867671691 to 2.1976549413735347 (median 0.4395) -- no physical unit (s, ms, us) maps this onto a plausible extracellular AP trough-to-peak duration (real values are ~0.1-1.0 ms regardless of cell type). PT_ratio ranges 0.0013329614368891 to 4329.257426489165 (median 0.590) -- a real peak/trough amplitude ratio for a single-channel AP waveform is O(0.1-3); 4329 is not a physically meaningful amplitude ratio.

Directly computed trough-to-peak from the raw waveform_mean array itself (units/waveform_mean, shape (357, 82) for this session, units='volts' per its own HDF5 attrs) for the first 5 units: argmin/argmax-after-trough gave sample separations of 58, 74, 53, 65, 70 out of 82 total samples -- i.e. the 'trough' and 'peak' are near the opposite ends of the snippet window, not a localized AP shape offset by a small number of samples the way a real spike waveform's trough-to-peak would be. This suggests either the waveform_mean array itself is not a clean single-channel spike-aligned snippet, or trough/peak detection on it does not correspond to the field labelled waveform_duration in this file.

No sampling rate for units/waveform_mean is documented anywhere in the NWB file (repo-wide h5py key scan for 'rate'/'sampling' under the file found only firing_rate, nn_hit_rate, nn_miss_rate, drift_rate -- none apply to the waveform snippet's time axis), so there is no way to convert the 82-sample window to physical time even if the snippet shape were trustworthy.

These fields (waveform_duration, waveform_halfwidth, PT_ratio, recovery_slope, repolarization_slope, spread, velocity_above/below) match the AllenSDK ecephys spike-sorting quality-metric naming convention exactly, suggesting they were computed upstream of this repo (outside jnwb) during spike sorting/QC, not by any script here -- jnwb.functions/jnwb.analyzers only ever read them as passed-in values, never recompute them from waveform_mean. The likely fault therefore lies in that upstream pipeline or a mismatch between it and this corpus's raw recording parameters, not in any code in this repo.

User decision (AskUserQuestion, 2026-08-15): do not build a narrow/broad-spiking classification from these fields, do not use waveform_duration/PT_ratio as features in the supplemental analysis at all. Proceed with layer/firing-rate/class relationships unaffected.
issues: Root cause not fully resolved -- upstream spike-sorting/QC pipeline that produced these fields is outside this repo and was not investigated further per the user's decision.

Any other current script/figure that reads waveform_duration or PT_ratio from the grand unit tables (omission_grand_units.csv, unit_layers.csv both carry a pass-through waveform_duration column) should be treated as equally uninterpretable until this is resolved -- not audited beyond this finding in this pass.
plan: Neuron-type/layer/LFP supplemental analysis (goal-neuron-type-layer-lfp-relationships-20260815) drops waveform duration/PT-ratio/narrow-broad from its feature set entirely; 'find correct waveform' from the original request is answered as 'not currently recoverable from this corpus's stored quality metrics' rather than guessed.
